source_text: Post hanc vero responsionem aliud ubi a me pulsatus fuerat, deluere conatur. Ego quippe postquam de parvulorum voluntate requisiveram, secutus sum: Sed negas hoc, id est voluntatem peccatricem inesse nascentibus, et dicis tamen esse sub diabolo parvulos, nec dissimulas per quid eos degere sub potestate illius arbitreris; ais quippe: Quia de sexus utriusque commixtione nascuntur, sub adversaria sunt potestate. Dictorum eius itaque testimonio patuit, ob hoc illum parvulos daemoni vindicare, quia de sexus utriusque fuerant commixtione prognati; per quod docui, illum nuptias quae a Deo institutae sunt, quae sine commixtione esse non possunt, diabolo mancipasse.
pass_a_gloss: But after this reply he tries to wash away another place where he had been struck by me. For I, after I had inquired about the will of little ones, followed: But you deny this, that is that a sinning will is in those being born, and you say nevertheless that little ones are under the devil, nor do you hide through what you think they spend time under that one's power; for you say: Because they are born from the mingling of each sex, they are under an adversary power. By the testimony therefore of his sayings it was plain that he claims little ones for the demon on account of this, because they had been born from the mingling of each sex; through which I taught that he had enslaved to the devil marriages which were instituted by God, which cannot be without mingling.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nuptiae; Blaise Christian marriage as God's work
LS parvulus; Blaise infants as Julian's test case

pass_b_english: After this reply, he tries to wash away another point on which I had struck him. For after asking about infants’ will, I continued: “But you deny this”—that is, that a sinful will is present in newborn people—“and nevertheless say infants are under the devil. Nor do you conceal why you think they live under his power. You say, ‘Because they are born from the union of the two sexes, they are under the hostile power.’” The testimony of his own words therefore made it plain that he claims infants for the demon because they were born from the union of the two sexes. Through this I showed that he had enslaved marriage to the devil, although God instituted it and it cannot exist without union.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
